overall: The AG resolved the complaint by informal action and found the Berkley Board of Assessors did not violate the Open Meeting Law, because the election and selectmen/COA discussions were not public business within the Board's jurisdiction.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a quorum of the Board deliberated outside a posted meeting when one member discussed an election and removing officials with two members of the public, with two others overhearing or informed.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the discussions could not constitute deliberation regardless of whether a quorum of the Board heard the discussions, and the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Board found the discussions about a political campaign and the Board of Selectmen and Council on Aging memberships were outside the Board's jurisdiction.
allegations.key_passage: Discussion of political campaigns is not public business within the jurisdiction of the Board.

allegations.summary: Complaint also alleged a Board member illegally used town property to meet members of the public about an election; the AG said this falls outside Open Meeting Law review.
allegations.key_passage: The Division of Open Government’s review concerns compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we do not review whether the meeting in a town office to discuss an election could be a violation of some other law, regulation, or town policy outside the scope of our review.
